data.why: Whombat does not accept audio uploads through the browser; a new dataset is created by typing a server-side folder path into a form field, so the ten Xeno-canto bat-call recordings already tracked in the repo under example_data/audio/ are used in place rather than uploaded, with WHOMBAT_AUDIO_DIR pointed at that same folder.

goals: register a folder of bat-call recordings as a new dataset so their metadata (duration, samplerate, channels) is indexed
create an annotation project and build a set of annotation tasks from the dataset's clips
draw bounding boxes on a recording's spectrogram to mark where a call occurs and tag each box with a species or call-type tag
mark annotation tasks as completed and review progress across the project
explore sound-event annotations (list, gallery, scatterplot) across the dataset to spot-check tagging consistency
export the finished annotation project (e.g. as CSV/AOEF JSON) for downstream ML model training

review.summary: The tree follows Whombat's core annotation loop faithfully: register recordings, cut clips into tasks, define tags, draw and tag boxes on spectrograms, track progress and export AOEF. The screens and the replay back every task. Before filing, it needs the stated evaluation and review/verify stages at least stubbed, the login phase removed, and the unreliable Shift+Enter and scatterplot claims corrected.
